_meta.description: TOU / seasonal gold set (residential, CA + US). Canadian values come from the published documents the in-repo soft-repair scripts were built from (OEB RPP Nov 1 2025 consumer page, NS Power May 2026 tariff book, NL Rate #1.1S July 2026); US values come from the utilities' own published rate schedules (SDG&E EV-TOU-5 Aug 2026, PG&E EV2 Jun 2026, SRP E-28 May 2026). Each tariff names its source in gold_source. tests/test_measurement.py fails if gold and repair-script sources drift apart or if expect_computable disagrees with the computable contract.
_meta.notes: Utilities without utility_id are resolved by exact name + state. Structured clock windows (period_start_time/period_end_time/day_type) and season dates must match exactly. expect_computable is the computable-contract verdict for the gold shape. Clocks and season dates are only taken from source text, never inferred from labels; each gold_note records interpretation calls (all-in riders, billing-cycle seasons, omitted fixed-charge tiers).

tariffs.name: Domestic Service Time of Use Tariff
tariffs.gold_note: Winter weekend/holiday off-peak rows come from the tariff book's Note 1 (NS_TOU_WEEKEND_NOTE) and are emitted by build_domestic_tou_seasonal_components(). Keepers created before that (winter weekday-only) are not computable (tou_gap:weekend@11/01-03/31) until re-run with --plan tou --apply. Holiday rows warn holiday_rows_require_calendar while utilities.holiday_calendar is unset.

tariffs.name: Domestic Service Time-Of-Day Tariff (Optional)
tariffs.gold_source: NS Power tariff book May 2026, p.6 'Domestic Service Time-Of-Day Tariff (Optional)' Rate Codes 05, 06, Board's Order column (not Jan 1 2027); riders: FAM tariff p.66 (0.156¢), DCRR p.75 (0.648¢), SCRR 2026 (0.000¢). Rate set equals scripts/repair_ns_power_residential_2026.py build_domestic_tod_components().
tariffs.gold_note: All-in ENERGY = book energy charge + Domestic FAM AA/BA 0.156¢ + DSM DCRR 0.648¢ + Storm SCRR 0.000¢ (same convention as codes 02/03/04 and 80). The book's clocks are weekday-only ('Monday through Friday, inclusive, excluding statutory holidays'); 'For Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory holidays, all consumption will be billed at the rate for 11:00 PM to 7:00 AM' — encoded as weekend and holiday 00:00–00:00 rows in both seasons, the same pattern as code 80 Note 1. 'Applicable in December, January, and February' is Dec 1–Feb 28 (Feb 29 follows Feb 28 per the consumer contract); 'from March to November' is Mar 1–Nov 30. The $20.08 minimum monthly charge equals the customer charge and is not modelled separately. build_domestic_tod_components() still emits label-only rows (no period_*/season_* columns), so a live keeper built from it is not computable until that builder gains structured fields. Holiday rows warn holiday_rows_require_calendar while utilities.holiday_calendar is unset.

tariffs.name: Time-of-Use (TOU) — Residential
tariffs.gold_source: OEB RPP TOU prices set Nov 1 2025 (province-wide; identical to the Hydro One OEB-RPP-TOU gold and scripts/repair_hydro_one_oeb_residential.py plan_meta('tou'))
tariffs.gold_note: Commodity only: OEB Regulated Price Plan TOU prices are the same for every Ontario LDC, so this is the Hydro One TOU gold under a second utility. Toronto Hydro delivery, regulatory, OER rebate and HST are not included; tariff_contract() warns commodity_only_bill_incomplete for OEB-RPP codes. Weekends and holidays are off-peak all day (OEB), so holiday rows warn holiday_rows_require_calendar. OEB resets RPP prices each Nov 1; refresh both Ontario entries together.

tariffs.name: Domestic Time-of-Use for Households with Electric Vehicles (EV-TOU-5)
tariffs.gold_source: SDG&E 'Schedule EV-TOU-5 Total Rates Table' effective 8/1/2026 (Total Electric Rate column = UDC + WF-NBC/DWR-BC + EECC) and the EV-TOU5 TOU periods / seasons table on https://www.sdge.com/total-electric-rates
tariffs.gold_note: Bundled (SDG&E generation) customers; CCA/DA customers pay UDC + PCIA instead of EECC. Weekday super off-peak includes 10am–2pm year-round from May 1 2026 (previously March–April only); the 8/1/2026 table post-dates that change. Weekends and the eight listed holidays share one schedule, encoded as weekend + holiday rows, so holiday rows warn holiday_rows_require_calendar. Base Services Charge is the non-CARE/FERA $0.79343/day; DRAH/FERA $0.39688/day is not modelled. No baseline credit on this schedule (unlike TOU-DR1/TOU-DR2, which carry an 'Up to 130% of Baseline' credit the computable contract does not model).

tariffs.name: Residential Time-of-Use Service for Plug-In Electric Vehicle Customers (EV2-A)
tariffs.gold_source: PG&E Electric Schedule EV2, Sheet 2 (Advice 7921-E, effective June 1 2026) Total Bundled Rates; Special Conditions 1 (Time Periods) and 2 (Seasonal Changes)
tariffs.gold_note: Bundled service total rates. Time periods apply 'every day including weekends and holidays', so rows use day_type=all and no holiday calendar is needed. Base Services Charge is Income Tier 3 ($0.79343/day); Tier 1 $0.19713 and Tier 2 $0.39688 are not modelled. The semi-annual California Climate Credit (-$36.18 in the August and September bill cycles) is a bill credit, not a rate component, and is omitted. No baseline credit on EV2-A.

tariffs.name: Price Plan for Residential Time-of-Day Service with Super Off-Peak Hours (E-28)
tariffs.gold_source: SRP Standard Electric Price Plans (ratebook with Temporary FPPAM, published April 27 2026), E-28 pp.67–70: Conditions A/B (on-peak and super off-peak hours) and per-kWh Total rows; each Total re-summed from its ten unbundled components
tariffs.gold_note: Per-kWh Totals are fully bundled (delivery, transmission incl. TCA credit, ancillary, system benefits, generation, FPPAM); SRP has no separate kWh riders. Summer and Summer Peak totals include the temporary FPPAM decrease for the May–Oct 2026 billing cycles. SRP defines seasons by billing cycle ('May, June, September, and October billing cycles' / 'July and August' / 'November through April'); the gold encodes those as calendar months, so real bills shift by each customer's meter-read date. Clocks are Mountain Standard Time (Arizona has no DST). On-peak 6–9pm is weekdays excluding six named holidays; super off-peak 8am–3pm applies every day including holidays, so holiday rows mirror weekends and warn holiday_rows_require_calendar. The Monthly Service Charge ($20/$30/$40 by dwelling type and amperage) is not modelled because the tier depends on the premise.
